# Kusajātaka (Ja 531)

**ID:** Ja 531
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Kusajātaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** King Grass
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja531
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0514m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kusajātaka* (Ja 531) is a major canonical birth story of the Pali Jātaka collection [Berkwitz 2013; Crosby 2014]. In the frame story, the Buddha narrates the tale while residing at Jetavana with reference to a backsliding monk [SuttaCentral]. The core narrative relates the tribulations of King Kusa, a Bodhisatta of extraordinary capability but pronounced physical ugliness, and his marriage to the beautiful princess Pabhāvatī [Cabezón 2017; Crosby 2014]. Their union involves the classic motif of a golden image used in a reluctant marital search, a narrative device shared across several Jātaka tales [Silk 2009]. Because of his repulsiveness, Pabhāvatī deserts him, but Kusa faithfully endures numerous humiliations, eventually rescues her from rival kings, and is happily reunited with her [Cabezón 2017; Crosby 2014]. Verses in the text also reflect social rhetoric and aspersions surrounding outcastes such as *caṇḍālas* [Silk, Rhetoric around caṇḍālas].

Beyond the Pali canon and its commentary (*Jātaka-aṭṭhavaṇṇanā*), the *Kusajātaka* was exceptionally influential in Sinhala literary history [Berkwitz 2013; Crosby 2014]. It served as the basis for King Parākramabāhu II's thirteenth-century classical poem *Kavsiḷumiṇa*, as well as Alagiyavanna Mohottāla's sixteenth-century *Kusa Jātaka Kāvya* (or *Kusadā Kava*) and the earlier *Kusadāvata* [Berkwitz 2013; Buswell 2004; Chandawimala Thero; Crosby 2014]. The narrative has also been the subject of comparative modern scholarship, notably Tilak Raj Chopra's monograph [Yuyama 1979].

In terms of parallels and text reuse, SuttaCentral records two distinct versions in the *Mahāvastu* (Mvu 65 and 66) [SuttaCentral]. The *Mahāvastu* transmits an earlier prose-dominant account in volume two and a verse-heavy recension in volume three that closely corresponds to the Pali verses [Jones 1952; Balasooriya et al. 1980]. DharmaNexus matches confirm cross-language alignments with the *Mahāvastu-avadāna* (highest similarity score 85), along with Tibetan alignments to the *Bodhisatvāvadānakalpalatā* and the *Vinaya-kṣudraka-vastu* [DharmaNexus]. Internally within Pali literature, DharmaNexus detects extensive shared material with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Vessantarajātaka* (Ja 547), and Aggavaṃsa's grammatical work *Saddanītippakaraṇaṃ* [DharmaNexus].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Resembling parallels (SuttaCentral): San Lo Mvu 65 The Kuśa Jātaka (1); San Lo Mvu 66 The Kuśa Jātaka (2)
- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Pañcamo bhāgo) (Atk S0514a1) (§20.4–33.4 ↔ §2365–2402); Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Sattamo bhāgo) (Atk S0514a3) (§79.4–80.2 ↔ §3499–3501); Byākaraṇa gantha-saṅgaho Saddanītippakaraṇaṃ (Dhātumālā) (Anya E0804n) (§48.4–50.1 ↔ §136–139); Vessantarajātaka (Ja 547) (§79.4–80.2 ↔ §38.2–38.4)
- Cross-language matches (DharmaNexus): Mahāvastu-avadāna (SA_K14_mhvastuu) [sa]; བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་རྟོགས་པ་བརྗོད་པ་དཔག་བསམ་གྱི་འཁྲི་ཤིང་། (bodhisatvāvadānakalpalatā) (D4155-2) [bo]; འདུལ་བ་ཕྲན་ཚེགས་ཀྱི་གཞི། (vinaya-kṣudraka-vastu) (D0006) [bo]; བསྒོམ་པའི་རིམ་པ་མདོ་ཀུན་ལས་བཏུས་པ། ([bhāvanākramasūtrasamuccaya]) (D3933) [bo]; ཀླུ་ཀུན་ཏུ་དགའ་བ་ཞེས་བྱ་བའི་ཟློས་གར། (nāgānanda-nāma-nāṭaka) (D4154) [bo]; 中阿含經 (ZH_T01_0026) [zh]; 中阿含經 (ZH_T01_0026) [zh]; 別譯雜阿含經 (ZH_T02_0100) [zh]

- [Silk, Rhetoric around caṇḍālas] Jonathan A. Silk, Indian Buddhist Attitudes toward Outcastes: Rhetoric around Caṇḍālas — Analyzed verses containing insults and references to caṇḍālas in the Kuśa Jātaka.
